claim: RapidFuzz: opt-in approximate edit distance from paper 121
why: The algorithm runs the exact quadratic dynamic program whenever ℓ < 2^1000 (ℓ ≈ log log N), so the approximation branch never executes for N < 2^(2^(2^999)). A faithful implementation is the exact DP RapidFuzz already beats with bit-parallel Myers.
check: Confirmed. sections/02-geometry.tex: "Use exact dynamic programming also if $\ell<2^{1000}$ or $\ell\varepsilon<10$. It uses $O((N+1)^2)$ word operations", with H = least power of two >= ceil(log2(N+2)) and ell = least power of two >= log2 H. So the approximate branch needs N+2 > 2^(2^(2^999)) (and ell*eps >= 10 on top), and thm:main is pointwise in eps with eps-dependent thresholds.

claim: Zstd: pack dictionary phrases with the SCS 2-approximation (paper 128)
why: COVER/FASTCOVER maximize k-mer coverage under a byte budget; the objective is not superstring length. Measured on a 17.8 MB corpus: merging the selected segments could save at most 1.05% (COVER) or 1.29% (FASTCOVER) of dictionary bytes, and plain greedy merging already captures all of it.
check: Confirmed. zstd HEAD 49cf517: cover.c:483-490 and fastcover.c:140-147 score Score(S)=sum of F(dmer) and zero the covered dmers, and both build loops fill until tail==0 with segmentSize=MIN(...,tail), i.e. coverage under a byte budget with no superstring objective; ZDICT_trainFromBuffer (zdict.c:1111) defaults to fastCover. A rerun reproduced the segment logs byte for byte, and an independent cycle-cover bound equals greedy: 1,186 B = 1.053% (COVER) and 1,452 B = 1.289% (FASTCOVER) of 112,640, so the method is sound (the '1.06%' equals 1186/111454, i.e. divided by the merged length, not the dictionary size).

claim: GMP: prototype a huge-operand backend from sub-n log n multiplication (paper 109)
why: The exponent saving is 2^-182 and the construction leaves its trivial case only at n ≥ 2^(2^(2^75)) bits. At n = 2^(2^64) bits the speedup is about 1 + 10^-53. There is no crossover to measure.
check: Confirmed. thm:main gives one multitape Turing machine with T_A(n)=O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), kappa=2^{-182}, and eq:fixed-parameters sets epsilon=2^{-75}. In 08-assembly.tex b=ceil(log2 n) and d=floor(b^epsilon), so d>=2 iff b>=2^(2^75), i.e. n > 2^(2^(2^75)-1), with "schoolbook multiplication" below the cutoff.

claim: FFTW: test the sub-n log n exact DFT in genfft (paper 130)
why: The saving is (log n)^(2·10^-13) ≈ 1 + 10^-12 in an exact-arithmetic model, the recursion only starts at transform length 2^(7.2·10^7), and it processes 2^71 arrays at once. The paper itself says there is no useful crossover estimate.
check: Confirmed. thm:main: O(n(log n)^theta(log log n)^{4-theta}) with theta=log_m(m-Delta/W_*), m=10^6, W_*=2^71, Delta=6871402692000000, so 1-theta=2.106e-13 and cor:decimal gives O(n(log n)^{1-10^{-13}}); the paper says "The constants in the algorithm are enormous ... with no useful crossover estimate". Wording nit in prior.json: 2^71 is the number of batched arrays, not a block length, and the recursion only engages for transform length 2^k with k>=K=72*10^6.
